effects.description: Pre-treatment of mice with exosomes from highly metastatic B16-F10 melanoma cells increased lung metastatic burden compared with control synthetic liposomes (Figure 4E).
effects.citation_sentence: We next used shScr and shMet exosomes to replicate an experiment that tested whether exosome-dependent Met signaling impacted primary tumor growth and metastasis. Synthetic unilamellar 100 nm liposomes were used as a control to test if tumor exosomes enhance metastasis. This experiment is similar to what was reported in Figure 4E of Peinado et al., 2012 and described in Protocol 3 in the Registered Report (Lesnik et al., 2016).
effects.evidence: Results, 'Exosome-dependent Met signaling on primary tumor growth and metastasis' + Figure 2C legend: 'Planned contrast between shScr and synthetic liposomes; Fisher's LSD test; t(16) = 0.543, p = 0.594 ... Cohen's d = 0.31, 95% CI [-0.83, 1.45]'; summary: 'for this experiment we found results that were in the same direction as the original study and not statistically significant.' Meta-analysis (Figure 3) p = 0.149, Cochran's Q p = 0.045.
effects.notes: Same direction, not significant; authors never say 'failed to replicate' but also claim no support, and note the replication point estimate lies outside the original CI. Coded failure under Step 2 (CI includes null, no support claimed); a second coder could choose inconclusive because authors list mitigating factors (shorter endpoint, higher RSD, weaker knockdown) and describe 'a small increase' (candidate luna56 did so). Enumeration: lung and femur treated as separate claims (original reported decreased 'lung and bone' metastasis; replication runs separate pre-specified tests and meta-analyses for each); liposome contrast treated as the claim that tumor exosomes enhance metastasis, not as a bare control.

effects.description: Reducing Met in B16-F10 exosomes by shRNA decreased the lung metastatic burden produced by exosome education compared with control shScr exosomes (Figure 4E).
effects.citation_sentence: The original study reported metastatic burden in the lungs of mice injected with shScr exosomes [M = 5.1×10^4 photons/sec; 10.8 log units] were reduced by 165.3% [M = 1.3×10^4 photons/sec; 9.1 log units] and 80.0% [M = 2.3×10^4 photons/sec; 10.0 log units] with shMet exosomes and synthetic liposomes, respectively (Peinado et al., 2012).

Cohen's d = 0.34, 95% CI [-0.76, 1.44]'; Results: 'To summarize, for this experiment we found results that were in the same direction as the original study and not statistically significant.' effects.notes: Same direction (36.9% ln-based difference), not significant; abstract: 'a small increase in metastatic burden with exosomes from control cells that was diminished when Met expression was reduced; however ... they were not statistically significant.' Failure vs inconclusive is the plausible disagreement. effects.outcome: primary tumor growth (caliper volume over time; excised tumor weight at end)
effects.contrast: shScr exosomes vs shMet exosomes vs synthetic liposomes
effects.timepoint: tumor weight at end of study, day 18 after implantation (volume tracked throughout)
effects.description: Exosome education (shScr, shMet exosomes or liposomes) produced no differences in primary tumor growth between the three groups (original null claim; data not shown).
effects.citation_sentence: This is consistent with the original study that stated no differences in primary tumor growth between the three groups; however, those data were not shown, preventing direct comparison of the original study results and the results from this replication attempt.
effects.evidence: Results: 'There was not a statistically significant difference between the tumor weights of the three groups (Kruskal-Wallis: H(2) = 2.85, p=0.24)... This is consistent with the original study that stated no differences in primary tumor growth'; Abstract: 'Similar to the results in the original study, we did not find a statistically significant change in primary tumor growth.'
effects.notes: Original null claim replicated as null and authors call it consistent -> success. Enumeration doubt: the original's null on primary tumor growth (data not shown) may be read as a confound check rather than a claim in its own right, and no original data/meta-analysis exist for it; a coder excluding it would code 4 entries. Neither candidate proposed it. Not coded as separate entries: Supplementary Figure 5A shMet knockdown of Met/pMet in cells (reduced, 'consistent with the stable cells reported in the original study') and Supplementary Figure 1C / exosome characterization (markers, Met present in shScr exosomes and reduced in shMet; pMet not reliably detected) — treated as manipulation checks/reagent validation, not claims of the original. If an auditor treats the exosomal pMet detection as a claim, it would be a failure (pMet not detected in exosomes).
